advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Harden the console-script admission to require a value argument immediately after `--basetemp` (and ideally that it derives from a per-parent path), not merely the flag string's presence anywhere in the argv.
evidence: tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py:147: `if shape is None or (shape == "console-script" and _BASETEMP_FLAG in atoms):`

Docstring at tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py:120 states 'must own its basetemp itself', but `_BASETEMP_FLAG in atoms` checks only that the flag STRING exists, not that a value follows it or points under the parent tmp_path.

ABSENCE: no check that the element after `--basetemp` exists/derives from a per-parent path; a console-script argv ending in a bare `--basetemp` token would be admitted as safe while producing no valid private root.
advisory.finding: For the console-script spelling, the guard admits a launch whenever the literal string '--basetemp' appears anywhere in the argv atoms, without verifying that a value argument follows the flag or that the value roots the child under the parent's tmp_path. The guard's stated invariant is 'the child's temp root', but presence of the flag token alone does not establish a private root, so a malformed launch (flag with no value, or the string present for an unrelated reason) is admitted as clean.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider whether name-collision (same local rebound to innocuous text) can mask a real dash-c pytest payload, and document or guard against it.
evidence: tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py:57-64: builds `bindings` by walking all Assign nodes with no ordering/scope awareness, so a later `name = "..."` overwrites an earlier binding used at an earlier argv site.
Docstring at line 54 acknowledges 'Flow-insensitive on purpose' but does not address name-collision masking, only inline-vs-bound resolution.
advisory.finding: _string_bindings is flow-insensitive and last-write-wins: it maps a name to the last static text assigned to it anywhere in the module. If the same local name is rebound (e.g. a real pytest -c payload assigned, then the name reassigned to an innocuous string later), the dash-c detection resolves the payload to the wrong (innocuous) text and misses a real nested launch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider re-asserting the `pydantic_ai.providers.anthropic not in sys.modules` precondition (e.g. via a small conftest assertion or a first parametrized case) so the anthropic isolation test cannot pass vacuously if the child interpreter's startup ever imports the provider.
evidence: Old payload asserted the precondition directly: "import sys; assert 'pydantic_ai.providers.anthropic' not in sys.modules; import pytest; raise SystemExit(pytest.main(...))"

New body: "completed = run_nested_pytest(tmp_path, \"-q\", node, env=subprocess_env())" then "assert completed.returncode == 0" — the docstring still claims "Each auth oracle must pass when the provider has not already been imported" but nothing now asserts the module is absent from the child's sys.modules.
This is a minor equivalence tradeoff: a fresh `python -m pytest` interpreter does satisfy the pre-import condition for these nodes, so observable behavior (returncode==0) remains verified.
advisory.finding: The rewritten anthropic isolation test drops the explicit precondition assertion (`assert 'pydantic_ai.providers.anthropic' not in sys.modules`) that the old `-c` payload ran before invoking the node, relying instead on the fresh interpreter to guarantee the pre-import state; if a conftest/plugin ever imports the provider at child startup, the test's named precondition ("passes when the provider has not already been imported") would silently no longer hold without failing.
